notes.title: 0.9.37b New Pontoon modifications and bug fixes
notes.notes:
• Pontoon modifications for the T-26 and Panzer II are now available in the garage.
	• All vehicles will now automatically adjust their gun elevation when on uneven terrain to maintain their original firing range as much as possible. High-angle fire remains an exclusive ability for self-propelled artillery.
	• Fixed a bug where the trajectory of high-explosive shells deviated significantly from the aiming line.
	• Fixed a bug where the BM-8-48 turret was not affected by elevation control — it's now easier to hit targets!
	• Fixed a bug where the range of the Bazooka Jeep, Maus secondary gun, and E-100 secondary gun was shorter than their stated values.
	• Fixed a bug where the target vehicle in the garage would suddenly start moving on its own.

notes.title: 0.9.02b Minor Update!
notes.notes:
• Mines in bushes have been removed! (Who on earth put mines in the bushes? Oh...it was me.)
• Hidden protection system is back. It was accidentally removed by the dev, and many players said they weren't used to it, so we're bringing it back! If you don't know what it is,  just know that it will protects you.
• Fixed a bug where enemy bunkers had turrets that didn't match their faction. Though honestly, captured turrets on bunkers don't seem too out of place...
• Fixed an issue where the blast radius of AI's HE shells was displayed smaller than its actual damage range.
• The difficulty display in the bottom left of the roadmap interface now represents the advanced difficulty level.

This update is mostly fixes and tweaks, but please go ahead and give it a try!

notes.title: Writing on the third day after release.
notes.notes:
Thank you for the support of all the players! The current sales of the game are enough to allow me to work on it with peace of mind. 
Although there are still some issues in this game, I will definitely solve them in the end. And I hope that you can provide me with more feedback and suggestions! Thanks!

notes.title: On the first day after the release of the early access version
notes.notes:
There were more players than I had imagined, and I am extremely grateful for everyone's support! 
Today, I have been collecting feedback from players all day. I apologize if I missed any replies.
In summary, I have identified three major issues with the game:

[list]
[*] Short game flow: Now my top priority task is to reasonably increase the length of the gameplay.
[*] Imbalance: Currently, HE and HVAP shells perform well, but other ammunition types, hull upgrades, and most vehicles have average performance. Additionally, weapon upgrades have minimal impact on low-rank turrets. I'm trying to solve these issues now.
[*] Lag: I will make further optimization attempts in the coming days.
[/list]

I apologize for these issues in the game, and I will now focus on resolving them.

notes.title: Multi Turret Academy early access version is coming soon~~
notes.notes:
Hello, I'm Zyf, a tank lover and the developer of Multi Turret Academy.

Multi Turret Academy is a top-down vehicle shooting game with roguelite elements.

After about a year of development and 4 months of public testing, I finally decided to release the early access version on Steam.

The game is priced at 9 USD(varying between regions), with a 10% discount for the first week~~

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44621799/5b8ac902bef347f0dbae833eac807dfc4c192704.jpg[/img]

So what is "Early Access"? As I know, it allows developers to sell unfinished works on Steam and recoup some funds to continue game development.

This is a great feature for developers, as some great games have been born this way, but it can also create a problem of developers abandoning the project.

As both a developer and a player, my advice to players is to judge whether to purchase based on the current quality of the game rather than promises of future content. And treat any future additions as bonuses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44621799/9577e8800f7c46325b851830397dea7c0acede56.jpg[/img]

In the case of my game, the main selling point is the availability of 92 selectable vehicles, including various well-known or lesser-known armored machines from World War II. Among them, ten are multi-turret tanks that are rarely seen (or very weak) in other games. If you are a tank enthusiast like me, this is definitely a quantity that will make you smile.

Those who have been active in my community should know that I have been updating almost daily for the past four months. The reason I chose early access is that I hope to transition to a long-term and stable update mode. With a stable source of income, I can update the game more comfortably.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44621799/848f3479986e33fac618ac014c7c5bd7cff9420b.jpg[/img]

Of course, promises need to be made. Here is the update roadmap for the first four months of the early access version of Multi Turret Academy.

I have listed the things I will definitely do each month and some things I will try to find time for. I have set aside the entire month of January to solve any potential problems that players may have, but once those are solved, I will move on to the next tasks.

In April, I will plan a new roadmap that will lead to the completion of the game. I expect a total of 6 months of updates.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44621799/edf0e77f3eaa9366520a7151f16f65f4a0d7f211.jpg[/img]

In conclusion, Multi Turret Academy will be released soon (January 18th 7:30 PM HKT, 3:30 AM PST)
I hope to see it completed together with all the players~~
